note: Planning ledger, not the repository release-evidence schema. Do not feed it to a gate as proof.

findings.title: Insurance-fund spending lacks custody-preserving constraints
findings.required_repair_from_audit: An authenticated state asset/UTXO identity; one canonical continuing output; explicit value conservation for each transition; datum updates bound to the action; real bridge verification or an explicitly isolated non-authoritative test substitute; claim lifecycle and expiry; deduplicated guardian approval state; exact approved amount/recipient; bounded payout; and replay protection.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Execute adversarial transaction-context tests that redirect funds, omit/reduce continuation, change guardians, inflate balance, replay claims, swap recipients and supply arbitrary bridge bytes. Every unauthorized case must reject. Independently inspect the compiled/deployed script hash and configured datum before any funding, even faucet funding intended as a custody rehearsal.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M3: M3.1b custody implementation and forward dependency provenance are independently accepted by R16, but Deposit remains unconditionally disabled because F05 authority, finality and replay are unresolved. The validator applies the shared finite five-minute contract, six unique extra-signatory cap, 16 transaction inputs/outputs, 16 non-lovelace fund assets and 896 serialized datum bytes; the R16 review independently accepted the R15 provenance boundary. No funding, deployment or Pre-Prod admission is authorized.

findings.title: Timelock cancellation does not authenticate DAO members
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Explicit authorized keys or authenticated governance state; distinct eligible signers; exact proposal/action and policy-epoch binding; required continuing/consumed state; normal delay enforcement; narrowly scoped emergency pause semantics; authentic finality evidence.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Arbitrary two-key cancellation rejects; duplicated/unauthorized membership rejects; normal intents cannot use emergency delay; wrong proposal/action/epoch rejects; boundary-time and repeated execution tests pass safely.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M3: CancelIntent still accepts any two extra signatories without authenticated DAO membership, action/epoch binding, or a required state transition; QueueIntent also accepts the emergency minimum without proving emergency authority.

findings.title: Governor permits voter-list corruption and weak intent binding
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Exact append/set transition, uniqueness, immutable-field/status preservation, one authenticated continuing state output, and action/intent identity binding. Define the voting-power snapshot or lock model rather than assuming repeated transfers across keys cannot reuse influence.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Dropped/replaced/duplicated prior voters reject; repeated voting rejects; wrong timelock datum/action rejects; state-asset substitution and multiple-continuation attempts reject.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M3: the vote helper checks one matching continuation but does not establish unique state-asset continuity or a snapshot/lock model, and execution checks only for any output at the timelock script rather than the exact action datum.

findings.title: Registry transitions validate inputs but not resulting identity/stake state
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Authenticate identity state and policy; validate actual asset quantities; enforce owner/identity preservation and metadata transition; require correct continuation or authorized NFT burn; constrain slash destination and remainder; bind evidence and authority.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: A declared-only stake cannot register; an update cannot withdraw stake or alter identity; an authorized small slash cannot spend the full stake; forged state assets and absent required burns reject.
findings.disposition_rationale: REMEDIATED: the accepted Option-B registry implementation and compiled evidence were independently accepted by the R6 review. The immutable fixture executes 49/49 rows and 67/67 evaluations with zero pending, with three legacy mint-side burn expectations explicitly reconciled rather than rewritten; supplemental compiled coverage is 28/28, migration 15/15, fixture 14/14, and provenance 21/21. Two pinned Aiken 1.1.21 runs each pass 120/120 with byte-identical blueprints. Raw UTF-8 DID bytes are preserved with strict 32-256-byte and round-trip validation; forward provenance intentionally resets to current lock 6f3b369ff5e7caf986ddf9b877af8bf1b71679307d90155e59f128313648d60f because historical lock bytes are unavailable. F05 authority, finality and replay remain required before post-F05 SlashAgent activation; Deposit and ExecuteIntent remain disabled. No deployment, funding, Pre-Prod admission or promotion is authorized.

findings.title: ICB and Mithril helpers are structural validators, not proof verifiers
findings.audit_severity_context: Critical when trusted for custody or governance.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Select an actual trust model. Verify signatures/certificates/proof roots and their chain of trust, source/destination domains, exact action payload, authority epoch, finality/freshness, and durable replay state. Otherwise keep bridges and their effects disabled in the release profile. An explicitly permissioned lab relay must be labeled and bounded as such, never called a cryptographic cross-chain proof.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Empty, random and length-correct forged proofs reject; wrong payload/domain/epoch/finality rejects; repeated and concurrent replay rejects across worker restart and host migration.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M3/M4: the Aiken ICB/Mithril helpers accept length/shape conditions rather than a certificate/signature chain, and the Python bridge path still constructs a zero-filled mock proof. No cryptographic cross-chain trust claim is established.

findings.title: TEE plugin can accept a fabricated commitment instead of a quote
findings.audit_severity_context: Critical when relied on as execution integrity; activation-dependent.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: A real, configured hardware-attestation verifier; authenticated measurement/report data; caller/root/workload binding; freshness/challenge; approved TCB and revocation policy; correct provider-specific quote format; and false/revert on unavailable backend. Test-only implementations must be impossible to activate as production trust plugins accidentally.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: The supplied authored Foundry regression must reject a plain concatenated-hash quote. Then verify authentic quotes and reject wrong runtime, root, workload, nonce, expired/revoked evidence and arbitrary bytes. The supplied Foundry tests were **not compiled or run here**.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M4: the Solidity plugin compares keccak256(quote) with an authored commitment and the Python verifier accepts proof length; neither invokes an authenticated hardware-attestation verifier.

findings.title: ZKML verification never invokes its configured backend
findings.audit_severity_context: Critical when relied on as proof of computation; activation-dependent.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Implement the backend call with a pinned interface and code identity, verify exact public-input serialization and model/circuit commitments, and fail closed on absent backend, false return, revert, malformed return or unsupported proof type. Model allowlisting is not inference verification.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: The supplied rejecting-backend Foundry regression rejects; one valid proof is accepted; tampered proof and each swapped public input reject; backend replacement obeys governance and invalidates incompatible evidence.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M4: ZKMLProofPlugin retains a configured verifier address but does not call it; nonempty structural proof data can pass after allowlist/hash checks.

findings.title: Gateway authorization has independently reproduced replay weaknesses
findings.audit_severity_context: High for a reachable authenticated control plane.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: One canonical, versioned request envelope; parsed key/signature bytes; finite integer timestamps; signed expiry, nonce and audience; canonical body and relevant query hashes; atomic shared durable nonce storage; concurrency-safe expiry; revocation. Apply the same policy to every effectful route. Existing VDSO replay abstractions do not automatically repair legacy gateway auth.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: The five failing auth regressions pass after fixing the relevant behavior; equivalent encodings cannot buy another use; duplicate concurrent requests produce at most one effect; restarts preserve rejection; body/query/audience changes reject; missing/NaN/Inf times reject before crypto verification.
findings.disposition_rationale: REMEDIATED after independent M2-R5 acceptance. M2.1-M2.4b provide the canonical signed request envelope, exact route classification, durable atomic replay/revocation, fail-closed SQLite schema validation, and the pinned Envoy live-ingress boundary. Real HTTP tests cover tampering, restart persistence, concurrent workers, handler-failure nonce consumption, revocation, storage uncertainty, and zero-side-effect denial. /nodes remains authenticated and the SPA neither calls it unsigned nor fabricates telemetry. INV-5 traceability is synchronized, mandatory frontend telemetry tests and the production-bundle credential scan run in CI, and the closed workflow-step validator rejects shell alternate-success forms. R3 identified the CI gap, R4 identified M2R4-01, and the checksum-verified R5 delta review accepted the corrected tree with no material finding and recommended F08 REMEDIATED and M2 COMPLETE. This disposition is not testnet, deployment, promotion, release, or production readiness; T06/history and M3-M9 remain open.

findings.title: Unrecognized environment names disable live-mode guardrails
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Strict enumeration at startup, explicit local/simulation enablement, unknown-value failure, one parsed immutable configuration object shared by all services, and deployment preflight that verifies the effective mode rather than only the text of a config file.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Unknown/missing live deployment mode fails startup; conflicting mock/provider settings fail; recognized testnet cannot produce a trusted mock receipt; CI tests cover every executable entry point.
findings.disposition_rationale: REMEDIATED after corrected-state independent M1 review: the typed VAMS_ENV contract parses all 25 registered M1 mock flags, rejects policy/environment rebinding, and covers gateway, Neuron, demo, anchor, and deployment-preflight executables before effects. Simulations are explicit non-live and non-authoritative; provider failures do not select simulation. The independent reviewer found no remaining blocking or material non-blocking issue and recommended M1 PASS and F09 closure.

findings.title: DA integration is improved, but receipt identity and route coverage remain incomplete
findings.audit_severity_context: Medium, with a live-release evidence blocker.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Canonical receipt type, strict field agreement, guard every adapter boundary, explicit live routing coverage, authenticated RPC handling, namespace/commitment/finality checks, and independent observer read-back.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Metadata swaps reject; no mock can be promoted; every enabled challenge type has an enabled route; independent reader verifies the exact committed bytes and inclusion/finality evidence during healthy and failure cases.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M5: live guards reject known stub paths, but Avail/EigenDA remain incomplete, canonical receipt identity and full route coverage are absent, and no independent exact read-back/finality observation exists.

findings.title: Cognitive synchronization reports success without real reconciliation
findings.audit_severity_context: High if used as GCA/safety authority.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Restrict this implementation to explicit simulation; implement stable versioned state representations, authenticated oracle observations and quorum/epoch rules, durable consensus output, actual finalized anchor updates, and real agent reconciliation. No anchor must be `UNKNOWN` or a bounded safe mode, not evidence of alignment.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Multiple processes agree on canonical state commitments; forged/missing/stale votes reject; partitions do not fabricate commitments; recovery retains policy epoch; global state actually changes to the verified result; safety-sensitive effects stop when valid anchor evidence is unavailable.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M6 after M1 containment: cognitive synchronization still lacks authenticated quorum, durable finalized anchoring, and demonstrated agent reconciliation. M1 now requires explicit non-live simulation, marks COMMITTED results simulated/non-authoritative, and rejects live construction and IVT sync before effects.

findings.title: Workflow demonstration and disabled interrupts do not establish durable live agents
findings.audit_severity_context: High readiness gap, not a flaw in DBOS itself.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Isolate demos; stable request identity; real selected-provider and selected-chain steps; transaction-sign/broadcast/confirm recovery; bounded retry and compensation; enforce policy before credentials/effects are released; checkpoint decision/intent/result linkage.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Kill workers before and after each external-effect boundary and before checkpoint persistence. Restart on a second worker. Demonstrate one authorized logical effect, one payment, preserved policy epoch, and correct refund/compensation after failure.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M5 after M1 containment: DBOS structure and isolation tests exist, but real interrupt/payment/provider recovery remains unimplemented. M1 now rejects those incomplete paths in every live mode before escrow, provider, payment, or recovery effects and confines deterministic demonstrations to explicit non-live simulation.

findings.title: Composed settlement is permissioned approval, not bound proof settlement
findings.audit_severity_context: High assurance gap; Medium configuration-denial risk.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: A proof/evidence verification call bound to allocation, provider, amount, exact intent/result, chain/domain, policy and nonce; strict configuration bounds; immutable or governed evidence policy; and a complete refund/dispute lifecycle. A GCA rejection must not be bypassable by simply granting a verifier role.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Invalid/stale/wrong-intent proof rejects; wrong provider/amount/domain rejects; a valid delivery can be paid only once; unauthorized verifiers cannot approve; all allowed fee configurations leave a valid bounded payout; expiry preserves refund ability.
external_blockers: F06/F07: authentic SGX DCAP and EZKL verification for the delivery back-end; every F13 test uses a noncryptographic fixture back-end
Phase 3 custody: the resolver (governance Safe behind the 48-hour timelock) has UNKNOWN signers

Independent release assurance remains required; bounded non-author AI source review of the five unpublished commits and follow-up is recorded in docs/remediation/repair_20261125/F13-LOCAL-SCAN-REVIEW.md
Resolver accuracy and availability measurement (docs/remediation/repair_20261125/F13-RESOLVER-ACCURACY-PLAN.md) needs an authorized closed canary
Hosted CI for the unpushed candidate remains NOT_RUN; local exact-range scans and source-bound native checks are recorded in docs/remediation/repair_20261125/F13-LOCAL-SCAN-REVIEW.md
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M4. Refreshed 2026-11-25 against local, unpublished b631f67; the previous rationale described 829ab54 and is superseded. Source now: verifyProviderProof and claimProviderShareV2 revert with LegacyInterfaceDisabled and no VERIFIER_ROLE path can approve or pay. Payment requires an on-chain challenge and the immutable deliveryVerifier; ActionDeliveryVerifierV1 binds provider, intent, workload, amount, nonce, issue and expiry times, policy root, version and authority epoch, chain and settlement target, and the settlement consumes the replay key once. Owner decisions 10, 10a and 10b add a 72-hour hold, a 5% bond with a 1 VAMS floor, at most 20 open disputes per agent, 14-day resolution by the timelock, binary outcomes, and on timeout payment to the provider with the bond forfeited to the provider; expiry still refunds unearned rows. The audit acceptance items map to passing Foundry tests (F13-SETTLEMENT-ACCEPTANCE.md, F13-DISPUTE-WINDOW-IMPLEMENTATION.md); local forge test passed 1287/1287 at b631f67, and hosted run 45383752005 covered d0bb4c5 only. Open because: every test uses a fixture evidence back-end, so authentic proof settlement depends on F06/F07; resolver signers are unknown; the bond ratio is uncalibrated (resolver accuracy unmeasured; testnet VAMS has no market value); bounded non-author AI source review is now recorded, but independent proof/custody/operational assurance is still absent; the latest repair commits are unpublished. Same-agent-family review notes (.tmp-history-tests/f13-review-20261125-01/F13-FRESH-REVIEW.md) are not acceptance evidence. Local source-bound scan/review and stronger test evidence are recorded in docs/remediation/repair_20261125/F13-LOCAL-SCAN-REVIEW.md; these do not accept F13 or any release track.

findings.title: Statistical anomaly detection cannot bear the claimed conscience guarantee
findings.audit_severity_context: Research assurance gap; High if treated as a sole safety gate.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Finite input/parameter validation; calibrated per-model/per-version thresholds; adversarial and out-of-distribution evaluation; privacy-preserving capture provenance; residual/OOD handling; explicit uncertainty; and separation of hard policy rules from learned warning signals. Closed/API-only models may not expose trusted hidden states, so admission policy must define alternative evidence or restrict their capabilities.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Report false-positive/false-negative distributions with held-out data and confidence intervals; test dimension changes, nonfinite values, unseen tasks and missing activations; prevent an uncalibrated detector from emitting an authoritative constitutional pass.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M6: the detector remains a fixed statistical heuristic without calibrated authority, provenance, uncertainty/OOD contract, or evidence supporting a constitutional/conscience guarantee.

findings.title: Compute health and declared cognition are not execution evidence
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Distinct states for discovered, reachable, authenticated, qualified, attested, executing and independently verified; one real allowlisted provider adapter for the first vertical slice; signed benchmark provenance; model/runtime identity; task and budget constraints; cancellation and result binding. CHC scoring should rank eligible providers after hard capability/policy checks, not override those checks.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: One real task completes with measured input/output/runtime commitments and proof appropriate to the claimed trust level. A merely reachable website or self-declared passport cannot satisfy provider admission or settlement.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M5: reachability, latency, registry metadata, benchmark values, and declared cognitive profiles feed eligibility/scoring, but no real task execution commitment or independent provider admission evidence is established.

findings.title: Release evidence is incomplete even before new defects are considered
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Fresh artifacts for the exact remediation commit, every enabled component and network; closed finding records; raw test and scan output with hashes; actual role and bytecode observations; chain receipt/finality links; independent reviewer/observer separation; and a signed assurance index.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: The actual closed-canary gate passes without manual status inflation, placeholders, unrelated inherited manifests or suppressing unresolved in-scope controls.
findings.disposition_rationale: REVALIDATED_OPEN for M7/M8/M9: current local evidence truthfully supports M0 discovery closure only. Exact final-commit reproducibility, signed assurance index, private-network/privacy/backup/drill artifacts, deployed code/role/datum observations, rehearsals, and soak evidence remain absent.

findings.title: Gateway lifecycle does not deterministically own background cleanup and economics keeper activity
findings.audit_severity_context: Internal test lifecycle and production shutdown reliability blocker.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Explicit application lifespan ownership with idempotent shutdown of cleanup tasks and keeper activity.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: Gateway startup/shutdown completes deterministically and repeated lifecycle leaves no owned background activity.
review_evidence: 20260921T200200Z-8233a726-f17-gateway-lifecycle-final (exit 0; record SHA-256 6c7c7035442af0259cf954db0be47099752b066a4e48ae2017b9128200489aa2; focused two-cycle shutdown regression)
findings.disposition_rationale: REMEDIATED: FastAPI lifespan now owns keeper startup/stop and cleanup-task cancellation/await; keeper stop uses an interruptible event and joins the named worker. The focused regression completed two lifecycles with no owned background task or thread, the 39-test gateway suite passed, and the 8-test keeper suite passed. The earlier TestClient/AnyIO hang was isolated to nondeterministic pytest plugin loading in the prior environment and did not reproduce under the pinned Python 3.12 test invocation.

findings.title: CI pins vulnerable httpx2/httpcore2 and bootstrap pip while pip-audit omits installed CI dependencies
findings.audit_severity_context: High deployment blocker for CI supply-chain assurance.
findings.required_repair_from_audit: Pin httpx2 at or above 2.12.0 with its exact httpcore2 2.12.0 dependency, pin bootstrap pip at or above 26.2, and audit the installed CI environment explicitly.
findings.acceptance_from_audit: A clean CI-equivalent install resolves the fixed releases; installed-environment pip-audit reports no known vulnerabilities; requirement-file audits remain enabled; and CI-only/bootstrap dependencies are covered without suppression.
findings.disposition_rationale: REMEDIATED after final owner review: the active workflow pins pip 26.2 and httpx2/httpcore2 2.12.0, retains both requirement-file audits, and adds one unsuppressed installed-environment audit. The clean CI-equivalent install, 39-test gateway compatibility run, 732-test full Python run, and three direct pip-audit records all passed. The absent hashed lockfile remains an M7 reproducibility gap and is not an F18 acceptance condition.
